Practice-relevant•Proposed Medicare Local Coverage Determination and evidence review•October 1, 2026

Noridian proposes noncoverage for AI brain-MRI quantification

A Noridian proposed Local Coverage Determination would make AI tools that automatically detect or quantify brain-MRI findings—including ARIA and volumetry—noncovered across its Medicare jurisdictions because the contractor found insufficient evidence of clinical utility; the proposal is not final, with comments open October 1–November 14, 2026.

Key label details: The proposed determination states that AI assistive tools for automated detection and/or quantification of brain-MRI findings are not reasonable and necessary and therefore would not be covered if the LCD is finalized as written.

ManagementMRIARIA monitoring

Added October 2, 2026 · CMS Proposed LCD DL40454; MCD LCD ID 40453, version 5

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

The draft draws a sharp line between regulatory clearance and covered clinical utility. Noridian concludes that automated brain-MRI detection and quantification tools have not shown that their measurements improve diagnosis, monitoring, management or outcomes beyond clinician interpretation. If finalized as written, the noncoverage position would apply broadly across Noridian jurisdictions and could affect AI-assisted ARIA workflows as anti-amyloid treatment scales. It remains open to evidence and public comment.

Study design

Noridian reviewed published evidence, professional guidance and regulatory information for AI software that assists with automated detection and/or quantification of brain-MRI findings. The proposed LCD applies the Medicare reasonable-and-necessary standard and discusses ARIA software and volumetric or neurodegeneration products. It proposes noncoverage rather than issuing a clinical-practice recommendation.

Key label details

  • The proposed determination states that AI assistive tools for automated detection and/or quantification of brain-MRI findings are not reasonable and necessary and therefore would not be covered if the LCD is finalized as written.
  • The evidence review found no randomized trials showing improved patient outcomes, no professional guideline recommending routine use for the covered question and insufficient evidence that automated measurements change diagnosis, treatment decisions or monitoring compared with clinician interpretation.
  • The draft was posted October 1, 2026, with comments accepted through November 14 and an open meeting on October 22. It covers Noridian Medicare jurisdictions, including multiple western states and U.S. Pacific territories, but has no current effective date because it is still proposed.

What changed

A Medicare Administrative Contractor has opened formal consideration of a broad noncoverage policy for AI-assisted brain-MRI quantification, including tools used in ARIA monitoring, creating a material but not-yet-effective access signal.

Strength of evidence

The policy status is authoritative for a proposed Noridian coverage action, while the underlying clinical-utility conclusion reflects a contractor evidence review rather than new comparative trial data. The record explicitly identifies evidence gaps, and the conclusion may change after public comment.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

Clinicians still must perform label-directed MRI monitoring and expert interpretation for anti-amyloid therapy. The proposal concerns reimbursement for adjunctive AI analysis, not whether MRI itself is necessary or covered, and it should not be treated as a final denial until Noridian completes the LCD process.

Field medical relevance

Important for imaging services, infusion programs, ARIA-monitoring workflows, vendors and medical-affairs teams separating FDA clearance, clinical availability, guideline endorsement and Medicare coverage.

Quanterix or platform relevance

The draft addresses software that assists clinicians by automatically detecting or quantifying brain-MRI abnormalities, including ARIA-focused and neurodegeneration/volumetry products. It is a coverage proposal, not a finding that the underlying MRI findings lack clinical relevance.

Access or reimbursement relevance

High but prospective. If finalized, the draft would establish noncoverage for automated brain-MRI detection and quantification tools in Noridian jurisdictions; it presently creates a comment opportunity and signals the evidence expected for future coverage rather than changing payment today.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Is Medicare already refusing payment for these tools?
This document is a proposed LCD, not a final effective policy. Current claims remain subject to existing rules while the comment and finalization process proceeds.
Does the proposal eliminate MRI monitoring for Leqembi or Kisunla?
No. It addresses reimbursement for adjunctive AI detection or quantification software. It does not remove label-directed MRI monitoring or the need for qualified clinical interpretation.
Is FDA clearance enough for Medicare coverage?
No. FDA authorization and Medicare coverage answer different questions. Noridian acknowledges authorized products but says the record does not yet establish reasonable-and-necessary clinical utility for payment.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Proposed, not final or effective
  • Applies to Noridian jurisdictions rather than all Medicare contractors
  • Broad technology category contains products with different functions and evidence bases
  • Evidence review found little direct comparative or outcomes research
  • Final language may change after the comment period
  • Does not determine coverage of the underlying MRI examination or anti-amyloid drug

Primary source

Noridian Healthcare Solutions. Proposed LCD DL40454: Artificial Intelligence Assistive Tools for Automated Detection and Quantification of Brain MRI Findings. Posted October 1, 2026.
